speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your baby's condition better, can you describe the feeding difficulties in more detail, such as whether he vomits after feeds and if the vomit is bile-stained or projectile? Also, has he passed stool recently, and if so, what does it look like?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, so the fussiness and tenderness suggest significant abdominal pain. Has he passed any stool in the last 24 hours, and if so, was it bloody or mucousy? Also, has he had any episodes of vomiting, and if so, what did it look like?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. Since there is no fever or vomiting, I am concerned about a mechanical obstruction or a congenital issue. Can you tell me if his stools have been pale or clay-colored, and has he had any episodes of drawing his legs up to his belly in apparent pain?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of normal stool passage and progressive distension strongly suggests a lower intestinal obstruction, such as Hirschsprung disease or meconium ileus. I will request an abdominal X-ray to look for dilated bowel loops or air-fluid levels. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with a gasless rectum are highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. To confirm this, I need to assess for the characteristic transition zone; have you noticed if any stool was passed during the first 48 hours of life, and can I perform a digital rectal examination to check for an aganglionic segment?

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of delayed stool passage, abdominal distension, and radiographic evidence of a transition zone with a gasless rectum is classic for Hirschsprung disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
